Definition: to urge severely, i.e. (figuratively) importune, embolden, capture, act insolently
BiblicalUsage: Rahab is to urge severely — to importune, to embolden, to act insolently. The father says, 'Go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend'; the beloved says, 'Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me'; and the psalm says, 'In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.'
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the word shows both sides of pressing hard: the friend who must be importuned, and the God who strengthens the one who cries.
